digest.top_line: SANO: 5yr OS 50% vs 54% (HR 1.17, 0.77-1.77) for active surveillance vs surgery after cCR to nCRT in oesophageal cancer; distant mets 46% vs 29%.
digest.tldr: Organ preservation dominates. SANO's mature 5yr data keep surveillance after nCRT cCR viable but flag a distant mets excess. In dMMR/MSI-H LARC, dostarlimab alone gives INV cCR12 68% vs ICR 47%, interim and single-arm. PE-PE: adding pembrolizumab to MDT (73% SABR) in omRCC improves mRFS 25.4 vs 11.0 mo (HR 0.47).

sites.intro: Mature 5yr follow-up of active surveillance after nCRT cCR, 43% spared oesophagectomy.

studies.name: SANO
studies.tldr: 5yr OS 50% vs 54% (HR 1.17, 0.77-1.77) for active surveillance vs surgery after cCR to nCRT; distant mets 46% vs 29%.
details: 🔍 Multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial, 2017-2021, N=309
🔍 Locally advanced oesophageal cancer with cCR after nCRT: no tumour on endoscopic biopsies, EUS, or PET-CT
🔍 198 active surveillance vs 111 standard surgery; median f/u 76 mo (IQR 67-86)

details.text: 📊 5yr outcomes, active surveillance vs standard surgery

details: 📊 OS similar across histologic subtypes; subtype HRs not reported in source
📊 85/198 (43%) on surveillance spared non-beneficial oesophagectomy
🔗 Extends the 2yr SANO report: OS non-inferiority at 2yr, better QoL with surveillance
⚠️ Distant mets excess under surveillance unexplained; OS CIs wide enough to hide a real deficit
⚠️ nCRT regimen, dose, and fractionation not stated in source
⚠️ Stepped-wedge cluster design: arm by hospital and timing, not individual randomisation; unequal arms (198 vs 111)

verdict.rationale: Cluster-randomised long-term data back surveillance over planned oesophagectomy after cCR. Stepped-wedge allocation, wide OS CI and the distant-met excess limit certainty.
verdict.audience: Locally advanced oesophageal cancer, cCR after nCRT

studies.significance: The distant mets signal is the read: 46% vs 29% at 5yr under surveillance, but OS still 50% vs 54%. Response assessment after nCRT (biopsy, EUS, PET-CT) now gates the surgery decision. Whether deferred surgery lets occult disease seed, or just exposes disease surgery would only have delayed, is not settled here.
studies.monday_clinic: For a pt with locally advanced oesophageal cancer and a cCR after nCRT (negative biopsies, EUS and PET-CT), this supports discussing active surveillance instead of planned oesophagectomy. It does not extend to incomplete responders or to a cCR declared without the full work-up.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial**, 2017-2021. N=309; median follow-up **76 mo** (IQR 67-86). Cox regression for OS and DFS, competing-risk analysis for distant mets.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Locally advanced oesophageal cancer with **complete clinical response after nCRT**, defined as no tumour on endoscopic biopsies, EUS, or PET-CT. 198 surveillance, 111 standard surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: nCRT was the shared backbone before the surveillance vs surgery choice. **Regimen, dose and fractionation not stated in source.**

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: OS and DFS **not statistically different** at 5yr. Distant mets **significantly higher** with surveillance. **43%** (85/198) spared non-beneficial oesophagectomy.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Extends the 2yr SANO analysis, which showed OS non-inferiority and better QoL with surveillance. Standard of care it challenges is planned oesophagectomy after CROSS-type nCRT, regardless of response.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents pts with locally advanced oesophageal cancer and a strict multimodal cCR after nCRT. Does not represent incomplete responders or pts assessed without repeat biopsies, EUS and PET-CT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The reported 5yr OS CI for surveillance (34-57) sits oddly around its 50% point estimate. Non-inferiority margin at 5yr not stated. No per-arm DFS.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Surveillance holds OS at 5yr and spares surgery in 43%, but the **distant mets excess** is unexplained. Neither the surveillance schedule nor any systemic strategy for surveillance pts was tested.

studies.interpretation:
The 2yr SANO result established that pts with a clinical complete response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy could defer oesophagectomy without an early survival cost. The question the 5yr update had to answer was whether that parity held once late regional and distant failures had time to show up. On OS it did: 50% vs 54% with HR 1.17 is not a significant difference, and the authors report the same direction across histologic subtypes. That is reassuring, but the interval (0.77-1.77) runs into territory a surgeon would not accept, so the honest summary is that a meaningful survival deficit has not been excluded rather than that equivalence has been shown. The source does not state the 5yr non-inferiority margin, which matters for how to read that upper bound.

The distant metastasis finding is the part that resists a clean story. Cumulative incidence at 5yr was 46% with surveillance vs 29% with surgery, yet OS did not follow. Two readings fit. One is that leaving residual microscopic disease in situ for longer allows dissemination that resection would have prevented, in which case the OS curves may still diverge with more follow-up. The other is that surgery partly masks or delays distant failure in pts who were always destined to relapse, and those pts die at similar rates either way. The authors count pts with distant mets within six months of nCRT among those spared a non-beneficial oesophagectomy, which leans toward the second reading, but the source gives no timing breakdown that would let a reader test it.

Methodology should temper confidence in both directions. A stepped-wedge cluster design assigns strategy by centre and calendar time, not by individual randomisation, and the arms were unequal (198 vs 111). Secular shifts in staging, response assessment, or salvage surgery quality over 2017-2021 could load onto the comparison. The cCR definition is also demanding: repeat biopsies, EUS and PET-CT. A centre that cannot reproduce that work-up should not expect the same results, because the safety of surveillance rests on detecting regrowth early enough for salvage.

For radiation oncologists, the trial shifts the role of nCRT from a pre-surgical step toward potentially definitive treatment in responders, which puts response assessment and the surveillance protocol on the critical path. It does not tell us which nCRT regimen, dose, or fractionation underpins these results, since the source does not state them, and it does not address whether higher-dose definitive approaches or consolidation systemic therapy might close the distant metastasis gap. Against the CROSS-era default of planned oesophagectomy for all, SANO now offers 5yr evidence that a selected cCR population can defer surgery. The distant failure signal is what to discuss with pts choosing that path.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: In cCR responders, nCRT now works as potentially definitive therapy. OS was 50% vs 54% at 5yr, but distant mets rose (46% vs 29%). The source does not state the RT dose or fractionation, so it cannot show whether the result depends on a particular regimen.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Planned oesophagectomy after cCR is no longer the only defensible path. 43% of surveillance pts never needed it, with no significant 5yr OS difference. The distant mets excess and wide OS CI mean salvage readiness and patient selection remain central to the decision.

open_questions: Mechanism of excess distant metastases under surveillance
Role of consolidation systemic therapy in cCR pts on surveillance

sites.intro: Checkpoint monotherapy as an RT-free organ-preservation route in dMMR/MSI-H LARC.

studies.name: AZUR-1
studies.tldr: cCR12 68% (INV, n=144) and cCR12+pCR 76% with dostarlimab alone in dMMR/MSI-H LARC; ICR cCR12 47% (54/116).
details: 🔍 Global single-arm phase II registrational trial, N=154 enrolled, NCT05723562 (ESMO 2026 LBA87)
💊 Dostarlimab 500 mg IV q3w × 9 cycles, monotherapy; no chemo or RT in the initial regimen
🔍 Data cutoff 20 April 2026; median f/u 26.3 mo (range 2–36)

details.text: 📊 Sustained cCR at 12 mo (cCR12) by assessor

details: 📊 Surgery after dostarlimab alone in 15 pts: pCR 12 (80%); composite cCR12 (INV) + pCR 76%
📊 98% of pts with cCR stayed in cCR ≥12 mo; no recurrences to date after cCR or pCR
📊 93% in surveillance with no progression after dostarlimab ± SOC; 71% with dostarlimab alone
📊 88% completed all 9 cycles; G≥3 immune-mediated AEs in 4 pts
⚠️ ICR cCR12 47% vs INV 68%: sponsor attributes the gap to later ICR confirmation; 38 pts still pending cCR12 by ICR
⚠️ Interim analysis, single-arm, no randomized TNT comparator; long-term organ-preservation durability not yet known
🔗 Context: TNT yields cCR 21–41% per abstract background; prior small dostarlimab study showed durable cCRs

verdict.rationale: Single-arm interim analysis with no randomized TNT comparator; INV vs ICR cCR12 discordance (68% vs 47%) and follow-up as short as 2 mo limit durability conclusions.
verdict.audience: dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer, treatment-naive

studies.significance: The ICR read is the number to anchor on: 47% (54/116) cCR12 vs 68% by investigator, with 38 pts still in cCR pending confirmation. Even the lower figure sits above the 21–41% TNT cCR range cited, which supports deferring chemoRT in dMMR/MSI-H LARC and reserving RT for non-responders.
studies.monday_clinic: In treatment-naive dMMR/MSI-H LARC, this supports PD-1 monotherapy with deferred chemoRT and surgery as evidence context for discussion; it does not extend to pMMR rectal cancer or to pts not fit for close endoscopic and MRI surveillance.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Global **single-arm** phase II registrational trial; this is an **interim analysis**. N=154 enrolled, median follow-up 26.3 mo (range 2–36) at the 20 April 2026 cutoff.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC)**. Further eligibility criteria not stated in source.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Dostarlimab 500 mg IV every 3 weeks for 9 cycles**, no planned chemotherapy, radiation or surgery after a cCR.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Key endpoints: sustained cCR for 12 mo after end of treatment (**cCR12**) by investigator and by independent central review, and composite cCR12 (INV) + pCR.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **cCR12 68%** by INV (n=144) vs **47% (54/116)** by ICR; **cCR12+pCR 76%**. 98% of cCRs held ≥12 mo, and **no recurrences to date** after cCR or pCR.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: 88% completed all 9 cycles. **G≥3 immune-mediated AEs in 4 pts.**

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The abstract places TNT cCR at **21–41%**; AZUR-1's INV and ICR cCR12 both sit above that range. It extends the earlier small dostarlimab study to a global registrational cohort, without a randomized comparison against TNT (as in OPRA-style organ preservation).

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer treated with upfront PD-1 monotherapy. Does not represent pMMR/MSS rectal cancer, which makes up most LARC.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The INV/ICR gap (68% vs 47%) shows cCR is assessor-dependent, and 38 pts were still unresolved by ICR. Salvage outcomes for the roughly one-third without a sustained cCR are not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The data support upfront PD-1 blockade and **deferred chemoRT and surgery** in dMMR/MSI-H LARC. Late regrowth beyond 12 mo, salvage results in non-responders and the functional benefit of avoiding pelvic RT remain open.

studies.interpretation:
AZUR-1 takes a striking single-institution observation into a global registrational setting and largely holds it there. The question it answers is not whether PD-1 blockade works in dMMR/MSI-H rectal cancer, which earlier small series already suggested, but whether the effect survives multicentre accrual, central review and a population larger than a single referral practice. On the investigator read it does: 68% sustained cCR at 12 months among 144 pts, and 76% when the 12 of 15 resected pts with pCR are added. The abstract sets this against TNT cCR rates of 21–41%, and even allowing for differences between trials in how cCR is defined and timed, that gap is too large to be explained by measurement alone.

The number that should move a reader's confidence most is the central-review figure, 47% (54/116). The sponsor attributes the gap to later ICR confirmation after the first end-of-treatment assessment, and the 38 pts still in cCR and awaiting their 12-month mark make that explanation plausible: if most of them convert, the ICR rate moves toward the investigator rate. The plausible alternative is that clinical complete response after immunotherapy is harder to call than after chemoradiation, because residual mucosal change and treatment-related MRI signal behave differently. That matters for practice, since a watch-and-wait programme runs on local endoscopic and MRI judgment, not on central review. A reader should treat the ICR figure as the conservative bound and the INV figure as an upper estimate until the pending pts resolve.

For the radiation oncologist the decision at stake is omission. TNT and organ-preservation strategies (OPRA, RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23 as the reference points for modern rectal management) all depend on pelvic RT as a main driver of tumour response. AZUR-1 implies that in the dMMR/MSI-H minority, RT becomes a salvage tool rather than a backbone: 71% of pts are disease-free in surveillance on dostarlimab alone. What the abstract does not report is what happened to the pts who did not reach a sustained cCR, how many went on to chemoRT, and how well they responded. That salvage pathway is what makes deferral safe, and it is currently a blank.

The effect size in routine practice is likely to be somewhat lower. Registrational single-arm trials enrol fit pts with protocol-mandated surveillance, and 88% completing all nine cycles reflects a selected cohort. Durability is the second unknown: the follow-up range runs from 2 to 36 months, and late local regrowth after watch-and-wait is a known pattern with other modalities. No recurrences to date is reassuring but early.

The result would be wrong, or at least overstated, if ICR-confirmed cCR ends up near 47%, if regrowth appears beyond the first year, or if salvage after PD-1 failure turns out worse than salvage after TNT. None of these is likely to be settled by a randomized comparison, since equipoise against TNT in this biomarker group is already eroding. The practical consequence is upstream: MMR status has to be known before any rectal treatment decision is made.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: RT omission is the decision this trial moves: 71% are disease-free in surveillance on dostarlimab alone with no radiation. The ICR cCR12 of 47% (54/116) is the conservative bound, and outcomes of RT-based salvage in non-responders are not reported in source.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Nine cycles of dostarlimab 500 mg q3w as the sole therapy produced cCR12 68% (INV), with 88% completing all cycles and G≥3 immune-mediated AEs in 4 pts. This moves dMMR/MSI-H status testing to before any TNT decision in LARC.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Only 15 pts went to surgery after dostarlimab alone, and 12 (80%) were pCR, which argues against routine resection after a cCR. No recurrences to date after cCR or pCR, but follow-up as short as 2 mo leaves late regrowth surveillance unresolved.

open_questions: Durability of cCR and late local regrowth beyond 12 months
Salvage chemoRT outcomes in pts without sustained cCR
ICR vs investigator cCR discordance in routine surveillance

sites.intro: Randomized phase II data on systemic IO added to SABR-dominant MDT in oligometastatic RCC.

studies.name: PE-PE
studies.tldr: mRFS 25.4 vs 11.0 mo, HR 0.47 (0.24-0.92), p=0.024, adding 1 yr perioperative pembrolizumab to MDT (73% SABR) in omRCC.
details: 🔍 Randomized, open-label, multicenter phase II; 2:1; N=85 (56 P+MDT vs 29 MDT alone)
🔍 omRCC after prior Nx, ≤3 metastases within 5 years of Nx or prior metastasectomy
💊 Pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w × 9 cycles (1 yr); first dose given before MDT

details.text: 📊 Outcomes and MDT delivery by arm (median f/u 17.5 mo)

subdetails: Discontinuation: PD in 11 pts, AE in 4 pts
2 pts G3; no G4 or G5

details: ⚠️ Local relapse is a listed secondary endpoint but not reported in the abstract; SABR in-field control unknown
⚠️ Only 29 controls and 16 control events; upper CI bound 0.92 sits near the null
⚠️ Two deaths total; OS uninformative at this follow-up
⚠️ RFS outcomes not split by SABR vs surgery in source
🔗 vs KEYNOTE-564: carries the adjuvant pembrolizumab rationale into SABR-ablated, later-recurring oligometastatic disease

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase II met RFS, but N=85, 35 events, 17.5-mo median f/u and a wide CI; OS uninformative with two deaths. Needs phase III confirmation.
verdict.audience: omRCC after prior Nx, ≤3 metastases within 5 yr, MDT candidates

studies.significance: SABR was the MDT in 73% vs 72% of pts, so this is largely a SABR-plus-pembrolizumab result. Local relapse, the read that separates SABR in-field control from new-site seeding, is a listed secondary but unreported in the abstract. It reopens the SABR-alone-with-surveillance decision in omRCC.
studies.monday_clinic: In omRCC after prior Nx with ≤3 metastases within 5 years, all treatable by SABR or surgery, this supports adding 1 year of perioperative pembrolizumab to the MDT discussion; it does not extend to pts with >3 metastases or without prior Nx.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Randomized, open-label, multicenter phase II**, 2:1, **N=85** enrolled March 2023 to February 2026. Median follow-up **17.5 mo**, 35 RFS events.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **omRCC** after prior Nx with **≤3 metastases within 5 years** of Nx or previous metastasectomy, all candidates for MDT to every metastatic site. Baseline characteristics reported as well balanced.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Pembrolizumab **400 mg q6w for 9 cycles (1 yr)**, first dose before MDT, vs MDT alone. Median 6.6 cycles delivered; discontinuation for PD in 11 pts and AE in 4.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **SABR** was the MDT in **73% vs 72%**, surgery in 23% vs 28%. Dose, fractionation and lesion sites not reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** RFS. Secondary: distant RFS, local relapse, OS, safety. Distant RFS and local relapse results are not reported in the abstract.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Any AE **80% vs 21%**, G3 **7% vs 3%**. P-related AEs 59%, led by hypothyroidism 23%; 2 pts G3, no G4 or G5.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: KEYNOTE-564 made adjuvant pembrolizumab SOC after Nx, including M1NED after metastasectomy. PE-PE tests the same agent around MDT where SABR, not resection, renders most pts disease-free. RAPPORT combined SABR with pembrolizumab in oligometastatic RCC without a randomized MDT-alone control.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents omRCC after prior Nx with ≤3 metastases within 5 years, all amenable to SABR or surgery. Does not represent pts with >3 metastases or without prior Nx.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Open-label, with **no RFS assessment method stated**; the 80% vs 21% any-AE gap suggests unequal ascertainment. Only 6.6 of 9 planned cycles delivered at median, and outcomes are not split by SABR vs surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: First randomized signal that anti-PD-1 adds to MDT in omRCC, **HR 0.47** on RFS. It does not settle whether the RFS gain converts to OS, or whether it costs the systemic-therapy-free interval that motivates MDT.

studies.interpretation:
The question PE-PE asks sits in a gap KEYNOTE-564 left open. That trial established adjuvant pembrolizumab after nephrectomy and admitted a small group rendered disease-free by metastasectomy, but it did not test pts whose metastases are ablated with SABR, nor pts recurring years after their kidney surgery. PE-PE widens the window to metachronous disease within 5 years of Nx and lets SABR stand in for resection in most pts (73% vs 72%). If the result holds, it argues that the biology driving relapse after MDT is micrometastatic disease that anti-PD-1 can suppress regardless of whether the visible lesions were cut out or irradiated.

The magnitude should be read through the trial's size. With 2:1 allocation, the control arm is 29 pts carrying 16 events, and the upper CI bound of 0.92 sits close enough to the null that a modest shift in a handful of control-arm events would move the estimate materially. Small randomized phase II trials that hit early tend to overestimate the effect a phase III later confirms. The point estimate of HR 0.47 is best treated as a ceiling, not a forecast. With two deaths across both arms, the survival question is entirely unanswered, and RFS in RCC has an imperfect record as a stand-in for OS.

Several design features should temper confidence further. The trial is open-label and the abstract does not say whether relapse was adjudicated centrally; in a population followed with serial imaging, an unblinded investigator call on a small new lesion is exactly where bias enters. The near fourfold difference in any-grade AEs (80% vs 21%) partly reflects drug toxicity but also hints that the MDT-alone arm was observed less intensively. Delivered exposure was a median of 6.6 of 9 cycles, so the benefit came from less than the protocol's full year.

For the radiation reader, the missing piece is local relapse. It is a prespecified secondary endpoint, yet the abstract does not report it, nor does it split outcomes by SABR vs surgery. Without that, one cannot tell whether pembrolizumab is acting on distant seeding, on the treated lesions, or both. RAPPORT explored the SABR-plus-pembrolizumab pairing without a randomized control, so PE-PE is the first comparative evidence, but it cannot yet say whether SABR-alone control is the weak link.

The trade-off is the one that makes MDT attractive in the first place: deferring systemic therapy and its permanent effects. Hypothyroidism in 23% of treated pts is a lifelong cost in a group for whom surveillance after SABR was a credible option. What PE-PE does not settle is whether earlier pembrolizumab beats SABR followed by systemic therapy at progression on survival. That comparison, with longer follow-up and the local relapse data, decides whether this becomes standard.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SABR was the MDT in 73% vs 72%, so this mostly tests SABR plus pembrolizumab against SABR alone. Local relapse is a listed secondary but unreported, so whether in-field control or distant seeding drove RFS is unknown. It reopens SABR-with-surveillance as the default in omRCC.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: One year of pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w, started before MDT, gave mRFS 25.4 vs 11.0 mo, extending adjuvant anti-PD-1 beyond the M1NED-after-metastasectomy setting. The cost is endocrine: hypothyroidism 23%, in pts MDT was meant to keep off systemic therapy.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Metastasectomy was the MDT in 23% vs 28%, a minority, and the abstract gives no RFS split by surgery vs SABR. Pembrolizumab dosed before resection showed no reported perioperative safety signal, but the surgical subgroup is too small to judge on its own.

open_questions: Does the RFS gain translate into OS with longer follow-up?
Is benefit consistent after SABR vs metastasectomy?
Pembrolizumab with MDT vs MDT then systemic therapy at progression

papers.title: PErioperative PEmbrolizumab (P) plus metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) versus MDT alone in patients (pts) with oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma (omRCC): The randomized phase II PE-PE trial
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract LBA88 · Proffered paper 2: Genitourinary tumours, renal and urothelial · 2026-10-25 · presented by Roberto Iacovelli (Rome, Italy) · NCT05578664

Background: Adjuvant P is the standard of care for pts with intermediate-high/high risk of relapse after nephrectomy (Nx), as well as for those with M1NED within 1y of previous Nx. Although omRCC pts may receive anti-PD-1-based combos, the optimal management of those eligible for MDT remains uncertain.
Methods: The PE-PE trial (NCT05578664) is a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase II study evaluating the efficacy of P in delaying tumor progression for omRCC pts candidates for MDT, including surgery or SABR to all metastatic sites. Eligible pts had undergone prior Nx and presented with ≤3 metastases within 5 years of Nx or previous metastasectomy. Pts were randomized 2:1 to receive P 400 mg every 6 weeks for 9 cycles (1 year) plus MDT (P+MDT) or MDT alone. The first dose of P was administered before MDT. The primary endpoint was relapse-free survival (RFS), while others included distant RFS, local relapse, OS, and safety.
Results: 85 pts were randomized between March 2023 and February 2026: 56 to the P+MDT arm and 29 to the MDT-alone arm. Baseline characteristics were well balanced between treatment groups. SABR was selected in 73% vs. 72% of pts, while surgery was performed in 23% vs. 28%, respectively. The median number of P cycles administered was 6.6. The most frequent reasons for P discontinuation were disease progression (11 pts) and adverse events (AE, 4 pts). After a median follow-up of 17.5 mos, 35 RFS events were observed (19 vs.16), with two deaths (one in each arm). Median RFS was 25.4 mos in the P+MDT arm vs. 11.0 mos in the MDT-alone arm (HR 0.47; 95% CI, 0.24-0.92; p=0.024). Regarding safety, 80% vs. 21% of pts experienced at least one AE, while G3 AEs occurred in 7% vs. 3% of pts in the P+MDT and MDT-alone arms, respectively. P-related AEs of any G occurred in 59%, the most common being hypothyroidism (23%), fatigue (18%), and diarrhea (16%). Two pts experienced G3 toxicity without G4 or 5.
Conclusions: The PE-PE trial supports the use of 1 year of perioperative P in pts with omRCC eligible for MDT, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in RFS with a manageable and consistent safety profile.

papers.title: Clinical complete response with dostarlimab monotherapy in dMMR/MSI-H locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC): First results from the global registrational AZUR-1 trial
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract LBA87 · Proffered paper: Gastrointestinal tumours, lower digestive · 2026-10-25 · presented by Andrea Cercek (New York, United States of America, NY) · NCT05723562

Background: Multimodal treatment with chemotherapy, radiation and surgery is a standard of care (SOC) for LARC associated with significant toxicity/morbidity. After TNT, the range of clinical complete response (cCR) is 21–41%. dMMR/MSI-H tumours are exceptionally responsive to PD-1 blockade: in a small study, neoadjuvant dostarlimab treatment led to durable cCRs and eliminated the need for SOC in most patients (pts) with LARC. AZUR-1 (NCT05723562) is a global single-arm trial and the first registrational study evaluating the clinical benefit of dostarlimab monotherapy in pts with dMMR/MSI-H LARC.
Methods: Dostarlimab 500 mg was administered IV every 3 weeks for 9 cycles. Key endpoints include rate of sustained cCR for 12 months (cCR12) following end of treatment (EOT) with dostarlimab alone by investigator (INV) and independent central review (ICR), and composite rate of cCR12 (INV) + pathological CR (pCR).
Results: At data cutoff (DCO, 20 April 2026), 154 pts were enrolled and median follow-up was 26.3 months (range 2–36). Of 144 pts with ≥12 months follow-up, 68% achieved cCR12 (INV). Of 15 pts who underwent surgery after dostarlimab alone, 12 (80%) had pCR, resulting in a cCR12+pCR rate of 76%. Fewer pts were cCR12-evaluable by ICR, primarily due to cCR being confirmed later by ICR after initial EOT evaluation. Of pts evaluable by ICR, 47% (54/116) achieved cCR12, with 38 pts in cCR and being followed for cCR12 at DCO. 98% of pts who achieved cCR remained in cCR for ≥12 months by INV or ICR, with no recurrences to date for pts who achieved cCR or pCR. Overall, 93% of patients are in surveillance with no evidence of disease progression after treatment (dostarlimab ± SOC) and 71% achieved this outcome with dostarlimab alone. The safety profile was acceptable: 88% of pts completed all 9 cycles of dostarlimab and Grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs occurred in 4 pts.
Conclusions: In this AZUR-1 interim analysis, 68% of pts achieved cCR12 and 76% achieved cCR12+pCR with dostarlimab alone with no disease recurrences to date. These durable responses indicate the potential to eliminate the need for chemotherapy, radiation and surgery, and redefine the curative-intent treatment paradigm for pts with dMMR/MSI-H LARC.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05723562.

papers.title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: Long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract LBA78 · Proffered paper 1: Gastrointestinal tumour, upper digestive · 2026-10-23 · presented by Sanjiv S. Gangaram-Panday (Rotterdam, Netherlands)

Background: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report 5-year outcomes.
Methods: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare 5-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis.
Results: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67–86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 34-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) were spared non-beneficial oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT.
Conclusions: Overall survival at 5 years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in these patients.
Clinical trial identification: The Netherlands Trial Register (NTR-6803).
